## Contract review (`CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, isolated seat, POST-MERGE) — objectui PR #8779 @ `a04441f7c9c5b322fd490234e1e6e7db5e6f5df6`

**Verdict: CHANGES REQUIRED** — a follow-up card is owed (F1 + F2 below). The card's original defect (a manifest claiming a licence with no text beside it) is closed on every path that writes a manifest; the ruling's fourth clause ("non-interactive runs take the default and still write it") is not met, and this diff regresses one cancel path into a crash.

Increment reviewed: `git diff 6cc48c4e4c^1 6cc48c4e4c` (squash, single parent `240c6059`), 7 files, +716/−7 — byte-identical to `git diff c03d03bb2 refs/pr-review/8779` (merge-base check). Evidence below is measured on the merged sources bundled with esbuild into scratch and driven through a real pty / pipe (`prompts@2.4.2`, `commander@15`, `chalk@6`, `fs-extra@11` installed from the registry), plus the same for the base commit as a control. No repo file was touched.

### Ruling conformance

Director-seat batch #91, option C (comment 5583986682), clause by clause:

| clause | status | evidence |
|---|---|---|
| the scaffolder asks for the licence | **met** | 4th prompt `License:` — `index.ts:102` wires `LICENSE_PROMPT` (`licenses.ts:388-394`): `type:'select'`, `name:'license'`, choices `MIT`/`Apache-2.0`/`BSD-3-Clause`/`ISC` (`title`=id, `description`=name, `value`=id), `initial:0` |
| defaults to MIT | **met** | `DEFAULT_LICENSE_ID='MIT'` (`licenses.ts:374`); measured pty Enter×3 → `"license":"MIT"` + `LICENSE` opening `MIT License` |
| writes the matching LICENSE text | **met** | `buildLicenseFile` reads `vars.license` (`templates.ts:558`), manifest reads the same field (`templates.ts:148`); measured MIT and Apache-2.0 paths agree in `package.json`, `LICENSE`, README, four headers |
| non-interactive runs take the default and still write it | **NOT met** | (i) Ctrl-C at the licence prompt → MIT + 10 files ✓ (measured). (ii) Ctrl-C at *Author* (or *Description*) → **TypeError crash, exit 1, empty `packages/plugin-<name>/` left behind** — regression, base wrote 9 files exit 0. (iii) stdin at EOF (`</dev/null`) or piped `\n\n\n` → **nothing written, exit 0, silent** — identical on base; `resolveLicenseId` is never reached. |

`@object-ui/create-plugin` `minor` — met. Option B not built — met.

### Derived judgments

**(a) Emitted file set / prompt sequence.** Before (measured on base): 9 — `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, `vite.config.ts`, `vitest.setup.ts`, `README.md`, `src/index.tsx`, `src/<Pascal>Impl.tsx`, `src/types.ts`, `src/<Pascal>Impl.test.tsx`. After: the same 9 + `LICENSE` = 10, one static key set in `buildPluginFiles` (`templates.ts:581`) so identical for every licence id (measured MIT and Apache-2.0; `licenses.test.ts:123-135` iterates all four). Prompts before: `Plugin name (without prefix):` (only without positional), `Plugin description:`, `Author name:`. After: the same three, untouched (the `index.ts` hunk only appends), then `License:` select as above. Dev/opus figures are correct here.

**(b) `resolveLicenseId` totality.** As a function, total: `undefined`, `null`, `''`, `'GPL-3.0-or-later'`, `42`, `{}` → `MIT` (`licenses.ts:405-407`; pinned `licenses.test.ts:98-109`). As a CLI path, the totality is only reachable when the run gets as far as `index.ts:128`. `prompts([...])` at `index.ts:83` has no `onCancel`; `prompts` returns the partial answers on abort (`lib/index.js:72-75`), so a cancel at prompt 2/3 leaves `answers.author` `undefined`, and the new `licenseCopyrightHolder` (`templates.ts:537`, `vars.author.trim()`) is the first code to dereference it — after `fs.mkdirpSync(targetDir)` (`index.ts:116`) and before any write (`:135`). On EOF stdin `prompts` never settles (`elements/prompt.js` registers no end/close handler) and the process exits when the loop drains. No `--yes`/non-interactive flag exists (`index.ts:150-156`: only `-d`, `-a`); the `licenses.ts:33` docblock speaks of "any future `--yes`". Agreement: on the CLI route `package.json.license` and the written text always agree (same resolved id). On the library route they can disagree — see F3.

**(c) Licence texts.** All four bodies diffed line-by-line against the sources the docblock names: MIT vs this repo's `LICENSE`, Apache-2.0 vs `bson@7.3.2/LICENSE.md` (202 lines), BSD-3-Clause vs `qs@6.16.0/LICENSE.md`, ISC vs `tinyqueue@3.0.0/LICENSE` — **exactly one differing line each, the copyright line**; Apache's appendix L189 is filled `Copyright 2026 Jane Doe`. Year = `new Date().getFullYear()` (`index.ts:130`, measured 2026); holder = trimmed author or `the <package> authors` (`templates.ts:537`). No stray `${`/backtick inside the bodies. `PLUGIN_LICENSES` (`licenses.ts:363-368`) is the sole source of both ids and texts, so no offered id lacks a text.

**(d) CLI options.** None added; help text unchanged; README `## Options` unchanged. Correct.

**(e) Exports / manifest keys / tests.** Package is `bin`-only (`bin: dist/index.js`, `files: [dist, README.md, CHANGELOG.md, LICENSE]`, no `main`/`exports`; tsup bundles `src/index.ts`) — the new module exports (`PLUGIN_LICENSES`, `DEFAULT_LICENSE_ID`, `findLicense`, `LICENSE_PROMPT`, `resolveLicenseId`, `licenseCopyrightHolder`, `buildLicenseFile`) are internal, not published API. No new key on the emitted `package.json` (`license` value now varies). `templates.test.ts:565` pins the sorted 10-key set; `licenses.test.ts:86-96` pins prompt name/type/choices/initial. Nothing pins prompt *order* and nothing exercises the CLI's cancel/non-TTY path — `index.ts` calls `program.parse()` at import and is untestable by design, which is precisely where the regression lives.

### Semver / changeset

`.changeset/8041-create-plugin-licence-prompt.md`: `'@object-ui/create-plugin': minor`. Right level — AGENTS.md:240 forbids `major` outside the synchronized `@objectstack` bump and maps breaking changes to `minor`; `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` enforces it; `create-plugin` is in the `fixed` group (40 entries). The only released package whose `src/` moved is `create-plugin`; no missing declaration. `Changeset Declaration` / `Bump Policy` / `Fixed Group Check` all green. Caveat: the changeset body carries the false non-TTY sentence (F2) and will become the CHANGELOG entry.

### Boundary flags

- Governed surface: none — `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test <7 paths>` → `NOT GOVERNED`; no `docs/adr/**`, `.claude/**`, `skills/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, no `content/docs/releases/`.
- Process: merged 06:42:59Z with `needs:contract-review` still on the PR and no verdict at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`; the in-seat review ran at `opus` citing the quota exemption, which `objectstack/.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/contract-review.md:60` denies to contract review verbatim ("契约复核 ⛔ 不适用额度耗尽豁免降档"). This review is the record.
- objectui#8778 (copyright holder line in the four emitted headers) — correctly filed, correctly out of scope.
- `Clause-②: yes` — **judged correct**: the CLI's emitted file set (+1) and prompt sequence (+1) are its published behaviour and the README documents both.

### Findings

- **F1 — blocking.** Cancelling at the Author (or Description) prompt now crashes the published CLI. `templates.ts:537` `vars.author.trim()` on `undefined`; root cause `index.ts:83` has no `onCancel`, and `index.ts:116` creates the target directory before `:135` writes anything, so the crash leaves an empty `packages/plugin-<name>/` that makes the retry fail at `index.ts:108` ("Directory already exists"). Measured: merged → `TypeError … licenseCopyrightHolder`, exit 1, dir empty; base → 9 files, exit 0. The PR body, dev report, opus review and landed note all state "a cancelled prompt … still writes the text"; true only for a cancel at prompt 4.
- **F2 — blocking.** `packages/create-plugin/README.md:66-68` (published) and the changeset body assert "A non-interactive run (no TTY, or a cancelled prompt) takes MIT and still writes the text". Measured on the merged CLI: `</dev/null` → nothing written, exit 0; piped `\n\n\n` → nothing written. Behaviour is pre-existing (base identical) but the *claim* is new and was never measured — all evidence in the PR was pty-driven, i.e. a TTY.
- **F3 — non-blocking.** `templates.ts:551-556` says the MIT fallback keeps manifest and text in agreement; it does not — `buildPackageJson` writes `vars.license` verbatim (`:148`) while `buildLicenseFile` (`:558`) emits MIT text, so `buildPluginFiles({license:'NOT-A-LICENCE'})` produces a manifest claiming `NOT-A-LICENCE` beside MIT text. `licenses.test.ts:162-167` asserts only the text side. Internal-only (bin-only package), but the docblock is wrong and the fallback silently manufactures the disagreement it claims to prevent; throwing would be safer.
- **F4 — non-blocking.** No test pins prompt order or the cancel/non-TTY CLI path; `index.ts` is unimportable (`program.parse()` at import, `index.ts:158`). 29 green unit tests could not see F1.
- **F5 — non-blocking (cosmetic).** README `## License` renders `MIT © ` with a trailing space when the author is blank (measured); dev noted it, rides #8778.

**What the follow-up card must fix:** (1) handle `prompts` cancellation in `packages/create-plugin/src/index.ts` — an `onCancel` that exits non-zero *before* `fs.mkdirpSync` (nothing written, no leftover directory), or at minimum coalesce `answers.author ?? ''`/`answers.description ?? initial` so `licenseCopyrightHolder` cannot throw; (2) make the non-TTY claim true or remove it — either detect `!process.stdin.isTTY` and take every prompt's initial (MIT included, still writing `LICENSE`), which is the ruling-conformant direction, or correct README.md:66-68 and the changelog text to the measured behaviour; (3) add one test that drives the bundled CLI (or an extracted `createPlugin`) through cancel-at-Author and EOF stdin so the emitted-file contract is pinned at the CLI level, not only at `buildPluginFiles`.

**Dev report `open_questions`:** none. **`deviations`:** (1) no `--pair` exit code — accepted, objectui has no `scripts/pm/`; (2) gates derived by hand — accepted, CI subsequently ran the full family green; (3) MCP `search_issues` substitute — accepted, immaterial to the diff; (4) `minor` not `major` — correct per AGENTS.md:240; (5) four licences, no free-text — consistent with the ruling and every offered text verified canonical, accepted (set size is the maintainer's call, flagged in the PR body); (6) README updated — required by Clause-②, but the added non-TTY sentence is F2.
